correctness.rationale: The b-divisibility of every nonzero palindromic reflection axis forces aligned zero-padding and an exact complemented preimage. Nonextendibility descends to strictly shorter palindromes; the reverse construction preserves it, so all maximal palindromic words are one recursive chain. Longest zero runs and their centers yield the base starts; exact dilation gives all starts, and valuation frequencies give natural density. The standalone finite checker confirms 1,050 length cases across bases 2..8 and 23,293 occurrence starts, but the infinite proof does not depend on those tests.

Allouche, Baake, Cassaigne and Damanik (2001), Theorem 9, https://arxiv.org/html/math/0106121v1: class-P palindromic complexity recursion; proof constructs the substituted palindrome by adjoining the common palindromic prefix.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2001 class-P theorem applies to the uniform morphism 0->0^(b-1)1, 1->0^b, so its general palindromic lifting map is already known and not part of the originality claim. It counts palindromes at each length and gives an eventual recursion, not an explicit all-b classification of language-maximal palindromic words, all zero-based starts, or asymptotic starting densities. These remain stronger content not directly implied by that theorem without the present lattice and seed analysis.

originality.rationale: A published base-two special-case length spectrum (Schaeffer–Shallit 2015) is explicitly credited. The arbitrary-base recursive words, exact complete start sets, and densities are not implied by the checked direct result; the other inspected sources concern different morphisms or palindromic statistics. Bibliographic coverage is necessarily non-exhaustive. The earlier class-P palindromic lifting theory (Allouche et al. 2001, Theorem 9) is also credited; the new mathematical claim is the exact maximal-factor seed/classification and its all-base occurrence/density laws, rather than a generic lift.

value.rationale: The theorem exactly classifies all language-nonextendible palindromes for a canonical infinite automatic family over every integer positional base, giving words, sharp length spectrum, every occurrence and natural densities. The support-lattice descent and complement insertion provide a useful structural mechanism not obtained by simply substituting b for 2 in the known base-two length formula.
